matches.context: This is the last game of both teams' November window in Doha. Kick-off is 17:00 local (14:00 UTC): Korea Times, Qatar Tribune and Star News Korea give 5 pm Doha or 11 pm Korean time, and footballpredictions.ai and Starting11 give 14:00 UK. South Korea are 32nd in the FIFA ranking and Qatar 60th (Korea Times). Both lost on 13 November. Qatar lost 0-3 to Australia at this stadium. Riley McGree (5'), Kusini Yengi (32') and Nestory Irankunda (40') scored, the first two after errors by goalkeeper Mahmoud Abunada. Qatar had three shots, all off target and all after the break, worth 0.06 xG (beIN Sports). South Korea lost 2-3 to Saudi Arabia, their first defeat by the Saudis in 21 years (Star News Korea). Oh Hyeon-gyu equalised in the 47th minute, Saudi Arabia scored twice in three minutes after 56 minutes, and substitute Lee Jae-sung pulled one back. This is interim coach Robert Moreno's sixth and last scheduled game. His contract ends on 27 November, and the KFA said it would judge him on these six games: 3-0 Ecuador, 1-4 Uruguay, 0-0 Venezuela, 2-0 Uzbekistan and 2-3 Saudi Arabia so far. Qatar coach Julen Lopetegui's side went out of the 2026 World Cup group stage (1-1 Switzerland, 0-6 Canada, 1-3 Bosnia-Herzegovina). They scored 2 goals in 7 games up to the World Cup (statz.ai), and Sports Mole says they lost the Arabian Gulf Cup semi-final to Saudi Arabia on penalties after a 0-0 draw. Both are preparing for the AFC Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia. statz.ai lists their group games for January 2027, while a Korea Times piece of 12 Nov says the tournament has been moved to December 2027. Head-to-head, South Korea have won 6, drawn 2 and lost 3 against Qatar (Korea Times). The last four meetings were split 2-2, and the most recent was a 2-1 Korea win in a friendly on 17 November 2020.

news.text: Lopetegui named a 28-man squad for Australia and South Korea, with Akram Afif and Almoez Ali leading the attack and Hassan Al-Haydos retained. No injuries have been reported.

Goalkeeper Mahmoud Abunada made the errors behind Australia's first two goals. Lopetegui made six second-half substitutions, and Qatar improved but managed only 0.06 xG. Yusuf Abdurisag had a late goal ruled out for offside.
Almoez Ali is Qatar's main striker, with 61 goals in 132 caps before the Australia game. Metcalfe dispossessed him for Australia's third goal.

Moreno said he would study the video of the Saudi defeat, that the fixes 'start with me', and that Korea have 'a chance to turn things around' on Tuesday. Korea JoongAng Daily trails a report that he plans to test young players against Qatar.
Son Heung-min, 34, played the full 90 minutes against Saudi Arabia. He hit the post, blazed the best chance over and had no shot on target. He is the record scorer with 59 goals.

news.text: Jo Hyun-taek was booked for a rough tackle against Saudi Arabia and replaced at half-time by Lee Myung-jae. No injuries were reported from the game.

The squad rift is officially over. Kim Min-jae, Hwang In-beom and Hwang Hee-chan had reportedly offered to quit the national team after the October win over Uzbekistan. On 12 Nov the five players involved issued a joint statement saying they had put it behind them, and Moreno keeps Son as captain.
Moreno's contract runs to 27 November. This is his last scheduled game, and Korea Times says the results so far have not done enough to earn an extension.

matches.context: Final round of Group A4. Portugal have 12 points (10-8) and are already in the quarter-finals. Denmark are second on 9 (11-8), Norway third on 6 (9-9) and Wales bottom on 3 (3-8). Portugal play Wales in Wales at the same time. A draw is enough for Denmark to finish in the top two and reach the quarter-finals (FootballPredictions.com, 101 Great Goals). Norway must win: they would then be level with Denmark on 9 points and go second on head-to-head, because they also won the reverse fixture 3-2 in Oslo on 24 September. Denmark would then drop to third. Neither side can finish fourth: Wales can reach only 6 points and lose the head-to-head with both (Irish News). Denmark can still top the group if they win and Portugal lose. Both would then have 12 points, and Denmark lead the head-to-head on goal difference (2-4 at home, 4-1 away). Matchday 5 on 14 November: Portugal 1-4 Denmark in Braga (Højbjerg, Højlund 2, Andersen; Bernardo Silva) and Norway 3-1 Wales in Oslo (Nusa 59', Schjelderup 68', Haaland pen 88'; Brooks 79').

matches.context: Portugal top Group A4 with 12 points (10-8) and are already in the quarter-finals. A point in Cardiff guarantees first place (RTP). Denmark are second on 9 (11-8) and host Norway (6, 9-9) at the same time. Denmark won the head-to-head with Portugal 6-5 on aggregate (Portugal won 4-2 in Copenhagen, Denmark won 4-1 in Braga), so a Portugal defeat and a Denmark win would put Denmark top. Wales are bottom on 3 points (3-8) and will finish fourth whatever happens on Tuesday, because they have the worse head-to-head record against both Norway and Denmark (Nation.Cymru). That also ends their hope of a top-three finish and a pot-one place for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw. Portugal won the reverse fixture 1-0 in Lisbon on 24 September with a João Félix goal on 22 minutes. Matchday 5 on 14 November: Norway 3-1 Wales in Oslo (Nusa, Schjelderup and a Haaland penalty; substitute David Brooks scored for Wales) and Portugal 1-4 Denmark in Braga.

news.text: Ethan Ampadu is suspended after being booked for a trip on David Møller Wolfe in Oslo.
FootballPredictions.com says Neco Williams is expected to miss out injured. No other source confirms it, and he is not in statz.ai's predicted XI.
Kieffer Moore withdrew from the squad injured before the Norway game.
Ben Cabango has served his one-match suspension in Oslo and is available.

Karl Darlow, Joe Rodon, Liam Cullen and Harry Wilson were recalled for the 3-1 defeat in Oslo. It was Rodon's first game since a hamstring injury at the end of August. Substitute David Brooks scored, set up by a one-two with Wilson, and FootballPredictions.com says he is pushing for a start.
Wales will finish bottom of the group whatever happens. Bellamy said the aim had been a pot-one place for the Euro 2028 qualifying draw.
Rúben Dias (booked on 46 minutes) and João Palhinha (87 minutes) picked up second bookings against Denmark and are suspended.

Francisco Conceição is still serving a three-match UEFA ban for his red card against Norway. Rafael Leão (hamstring), Nuno Tavares and Tomás Araújo withdrew injured, and Nuno Mendes was not called up because of injury.
João Cancelo is available again after serving his suspension against Denmark. He was limited in training on 10 November, working in the gym and running alone.
Renato Veiga, Rúben Neves, Bruno Fernandes, Vitinha and Bernardo Silva are one booking from missing the first leg of the quarter-final in March. Portugal need a point to be sure of first place.

matches.context: This is the last round of Group B2. Northern Ireland lead on 11 points (W3 D2, 5-0) and are the only side in the competition yet to concede. Hungary are second on 10 (W3 D1 L1, 5-2). Ukraine (4) and Georgia (2), who meet today, can no longer catch either of them. The group winner is promoted to League A and the runner-up goes to a promotion play-off in March. A draw is enough for Northern Ireland, while Hungary need a win. The reverse fixture at Windsor Park on 28 September ended 0-0: Hungary had 64% of the ball and 13 shots to 10, but Northern Ireland had 3 on target to 1. On 14 November, Hungary won 2-0 in Tbilisi (Lasha Dvali own goal from a Roland Sallai header on 73', then Barnabás Varga on 85'; Szoboszlai set up both). Northern Ireland beat Ukraine 1-0 in Belfast (Terry Devlin, 68') for their fifth straight clean sheet. Northern Ireland are without the suspended Jamie Donley, and Michael O'Neill will watch from the stands after his own booking.

Northern Ireland (11) and Hungary (10) play each other at the same time to decide first place. This game decides third and fourth: Georgia must win to finish above Ukraine, and a draw or a Ukraine win keeps Ukraine third. Third place stays in League B, and the bottom side goes into a relegation play-off against a League C runner-up (Liga.net; Flashscore). On 14 November Northern Ireland beat Ukraine 1-0 in Belfast (Terry Devlin, 68'). Northern Ireland had 15 shots to Ukraine's 7, although Ukraine had 62% of the ball. Georgia lost 0-2 at home to Hungary (Lasha Dvali own goal 73', Barnabás Varga 85'). Ukraine have lost three games in a row and scored once in their last four. Georgia have not scored in five group games. The reverse fixture in Tbilisi on 28 September ended 0-0, with Georgia taking 14 shots to Ukraine's 7. Ukraine play their home games abroad. matches.context: Sweden have won Group B4 and promotion to League A. They have 13 points from five games (10-5) after a 3-2 home win over Bosnia and Herzegovina on 14 November: Daniel Svensson scored after 5 minutes and Viktor Gyökeres scored two penalties, with Armin Gigović and Sead Kolašinac replying. Bosnia (8 points) are sure of second. Poland are third on 4 points (8-6) after losing 2-1 in Romania on 14 November. Romania scored twice in four minutes, and Marcel Reguła got Poland's goal. Romania have 3 points (5-14) and play in Bosnia at the same time. A win keeps Poland third whatever happens in that game. If Romania win and Poland do not, Poland finish bottom and go into a relegation play-off in March to stay in League B. Poland lead Romania on head-to-head (6-0 and 1-2), so they also stay third if Romania fail to win. Sweden won the reverse fixture 3-1 in Solna on 28 September: Benjamin Nygren, Yasin Ayari and Gyökeres scored, and Sebastian Szymański scored for Poland. Sweden also beat Poland 3-2 in the World Cup play-off final on 31 March. Graham Potter says Sweden will pick the team that gives them the best chance of winning.

news.text: Matty Cash has concussion from the Romania game. Arkadiusz Pyrka (St. Pauli) is expected to replace him at right-back.
Jakub Kiwior is suspended after reaching the yellow-card limit and has gone back to Porto.
Przemysław Frankowski is injured and has left the squad. Pyrka was called up to replace him.
Piotr Zieliński missed the Romania game with a foot injury. He trained partly with the team and partly on his own, and Urban said Tuesday's session would decide. Both Polish predicted XIs start him.
Jan Bednarek is available again after his suspension and is expected to partner Kacper Potulski in central defence.
Sławomir Abramowicz may make his debut in goal in place of Bartłomiej Drągowski.
Lewandowski was substituted in Romania. Urban said they had agreed to talk about his minutes and that he wants to try other players, including in attack.
Urban said a defender was badly positioned for Dennis Man's counter-attack that led to Romania's second goal, and called it another game Poland lost through their own fault.
Benjamin Nygren missed Monday's training with a heel problem and is on an individual programme. He travelled to Wrocław. He scored in the reverse fixture.
Lucas Bergvall, Emil Holm, Carl Starfelt and Isak Hien were injured when the squad was named, and Besfort Zeneli withdrew on 9 November.

Sweden have already won the group. Potter said he will pick the team that gives Sweden the best chance of winning. He did not say whether he will make changes. Kulusevski, back after a long injury, is planned to play about 30 minutes, as he did against Bosnia.
No Swedish suspensions have been reported. Sweden picked up one yellow card against Bosnia.

matches.context: After five games Group B4 stands: Sweden 13 points (10-5), Bosnia and Herzegovina 8 (8-6), Poland 4 (8-6), Romania 3 (5-14). On 14 November Sweden beat Bosnia 3-2 in Solna to win the group and promotion to League A. Daniel Svensson headed in and Viktor Gyökeres scored two penalties, and Armin Gigović and Sead Kolašinac replied with headers in the second half. The same night Romania beat Poland 2-1 in Bucharest for their first points of the campaign: Alexandru Cicâldău scored on 68 minutes with a deflected shot, Dennis Man added a second on 72 and Poland pulled one back on 82. That result means Bosnia are sure of second place and a play-off against a League A side, so this game cannot change their position. Romania are a point behind Poland, who play in Sweden at the same time. Poland lead the head-to-head (6-0 and 1-2, 7-2 on aggregate), so Romania finish third only if they win and Poland fail to win. In League B, third place goes into a play-off against a League C runner-up and fourth is relegated to League C. Bosnia won the reverse fixture 4-2 in Bucharest on 28 September: Gigović (12'), Tarik Muharemović (19'), Haris Tabaković (40') and Ermin Mahmić (55') scored for Bosnia, and Daniel Bîrligea (28') and Cicâldău (62') for Romania.

news.text: Striker Haris Tabaković was injured in the first half in Sweden and replaced by Ermin Mahmić. No update on his fitness was found, and statz.ai's predicted XI leaves him out.
Defender Tarik Muharemović is available again after serving his suspension against Sweden. He scored in the 4-2 win in Bucharest.
Dennis Hadžikadunić was reported to have a calf injury before the Sweden game. Forza Football said this was not officially confirmed as of 12 November.

No Bosnia player was reported booked into a ban in Sweden: neither the Flashscore report nor the SportsDunia ratings mention a booking. Bosnia are already sure of second place and a play-off against a League A side.
Edin Džeko has retired from international football. Kerim Alajbegović leads Bosnia's Nations League figures with 6 shots on target and 2 assists, and Gigović has 2 goals.

news.text: Midfielder Tudor Băluță is suspended after a yellow card early in the second half against Poland. Hagi: 'Băluță won't be there, but we have others; we have to find solutions.'
Nicolae Stanciu (calf) and Valentin Mihăilă (calf) withdrew from the squad before the Poland game.
Răzvan Marin missed the Poland game through suspension and is available again.

Hagi said there would 'probably' be changes and that Romania 'are going to play for the win; we know it is very hard, they are a good team'. Ionuț Radu is not in the squad and Otto Hindrich keeps goal.

The 2-1 win over Poland ended a run of four straight defeats. Romania have kept no clean sheet in five group games, and statz.ai says they average the most cards in the competition (3.6 a game) and the third-most fouls (15.8).
